chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
There has never been and will not be any believer up until the Resurrection Day for whom there is no neighbor who will bother him.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about neighbors bothering believers?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* underscores the universality of the 'neighborly trial' (*fitnat al-jarr*) as a perpetual condition for believers until the Day of Resurrection. It reflects the Shia emphasis on patience (*sabr*) and moral conduct in daily social interactions, framing neighborly friction not as an anomaly but as an inevitable spiritual test. The narration serves as a reminder that even the righteous are not exempt from interpersonal annoyances, thereby encouraging resilience in communal life.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-59 According to the same documentation, God’s Prophet (S) said, “
There has never been and will not be any believer up until the Resurrection Day for whom there is no neighbor who will bother him.”
